Subject: [ALERT] Borealis Analytics — sudden throughput spike + 5xx rate (need exec runway)

Team,

Alerting just flagged a sustained throughput surge on the Borealis account starting ~14:20 PT with a concurrent spike in 5xxs on our text-generation endpoints (critical route: /v1/generate). Latency for their high-priority route is reporting 5–18s and error rate jumped to ~6% (baseline ~0.3%). This coincides with their increased traffic pattern but the shape looks abnormal vs historical (sharp ramp).

Immediate asks:
- Can we stand a 30m exec-level bridge now? Recommend 15:30 PT.
- Engineering: capture live traces + slow logs.
- Product/CS: prepare a short customer-facing update we can send in 30–45m.

Related telemetry: https://console.redwood.ai/telemetry/trace?request_id=br-req-9842
Attachment: throughput_spike_20261130.png (image/png, 48KB)

I will open an incident channel and pull SRE and model infra. Please flag if immediate rollback is necessary — I want leadership alignment before we propose customer-impacting actions (credits/rollback).

— Mina

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 3:12 PM Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team,
> Alerting just flagged a sustained throughput surge on the Borealis account starting ~14:20 PT ...

Acknowledged — joining. Putting a 30m bridge on calendar for 15:30 PT and paging SRE, model infra, and runtime on-call. Initial hypotheses:
- Regression in client-side batching (they might have moved to larger batches) interacting poorly with our autoscaler.
- New quantization/profile we shipped for cost optimization could be degrading tail latency under burst.
- Unexpected backend queueing due to degraded pod warm-up (KV cache warm).

Action items I want covered on the call:
1) Live QPS and per-instance CPU/GPU utilization.
2) 5xx stack traces and earliest request ids.
3) Fast mitigation plan (rate-limiting, smaller default batch for this customer, or model rollback).

Customer-facing update: 2–3 bullets, ETA for next update (we should commit to 45m).

— Ben

Thanks for the quick ping. We started seeing failures at ~14:22 PT. Our SDK logs show heavy batched inference jobs kicked off at 14:20 (internal job id br-batch-772). Impact: our frontline product experiences degraded user flows — about ~25% of requests timeout or error for that route.

Sample request ids: br-req-9842, br-req-9847, br-req-9859. We need an ETA — this is affecting a customer demo at 17:00 PT today.

We will join any bridge.

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Borealis Analytics — sudden throughput spike + 5xx rate (need exec runway)

We stood the bridge — SRE and runtime confirmed: a recent model config (quantization profile alpha-3) was rolled to some of their dedicated nodes earlier today as part of a cost experiment. Under burst it increases kernel contention leading to degraded CPU-GPU handoffs; this explains the tail latency and 5xx pattern.

Immediate mitigations in progress:
- Rolling back alpha-3 on Borealis nodes (target 15:50 PT).
- Throttling client batch sizes for their routing key to conservative defaults.
- Enabling extra pod warm-up (prefetching KV entries).

Requesting exec approval for two customer-impact items:
1) Manual rollback of the quantization profile (expected impact: ~10–15m to start, 20–30m to normalize).
2) Offer a goodwill credit for today's incident (recommendation: one week of hosted usage credit).

Attachment: rollback_playbook_20261130.pdf (application/pdf, 110KB)

If leadership approves, we'll proceed immediately — rollback is the fastest, lowest-risk path.

— Priyom

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood status update — Borealis incident, mitigation steps and next actions

Sofia / James,

Quick update from Redwood: we detected a throughput surge and elevated 5xx rate starting ~14:20 PT on 2026-11-30. Root cause analysis (initial): an experimental quantization profile (alpha-3) was deployed to a subset of Borealis-dedicated nodes; under burst traffic it caused tail kernel contention and increased error rates.

What we did (mitigation):
- Immediately rolled back the alpha-3 profile from Borealis nodes (rollback completed; normalization observed within 30–45m).
- Applied temporary conservative throttling to your client batch size for the affected routing key to reduce tail latency.
- Enabled extra pod warm-up and increased instance warm pool for the next 2 hours.

Impact and ETA: performance metrics have returned to baseline for most routes; we will monitor for the next 12 hours and provide hourly snapshots. A full RCA will be delivered within 72 hours.

Compensation: as discussed internally, we will apply a goodwill credit equivalent to one week of hosted usage to your account; our finance team will follow up with the details and timing.

Next steps:
- 17:00 PT: brief check-in to confirm your demo path is stable (we will join to observe).
- Within 72 hours: cross-functional RCA and remediation plan.

We are sorry for the disruption and appreciate your patience. If you need anything before the 17:00 check-in, reach out to me directly (grace.oconnor@redwood.ai).

— Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
